content_voiceover: This slide covers prognostic scoring systems for follicular lymphoma. The FLIPI, or Follicular Lymphoma International Prognostic Index, comes in two versions. FLIPI-1 uses five adverse factors, easily remembered by the mnemonic No LASH, meaning number of nodal sites greater than four, elevated LDH, age over sixty, advanced stage III or IV, and hemoglobin under twelve. Patients with zero to one factor are low risk, two factors intermediate risk, and three to five factors high risk. FLIPI-2 modifies this slightly, replacing nodal site number with maximal lymph node diameter over six centimeters, replacing LDH with beta-2 microglobulin, and replacing Ann Arbor stage with bone marrow involvement. On the right, the PRIMA-PI score is a simpler two-step tool using beta-2 microglobulin and bone marrow involvement. If beta-2 microglobulin is above three milligrams per liter, the patient is high risk. If it's three or below, bone marrow involvement determines whether the patient is intermediate or low risk. For boards, remember No LASH for FLIPI-1 and know that PRIMA-PI is a streamlined alternative built around beta-2 microglobulin and marrow status.
keypoints: FLIPI-1 mnemonic: No LASH, nodal sites, LDH, age, stage, hemoglobin
FLIPI-2 swaps in lymph node size, beta-2 microglobulin, marrow involvement
Risk groups: zero to one low, two intermediate, three to five high
PRIMA-PI uses beta-2 microglobulin plus marrow involvement
keypoint_voiceover: Remember FLIPI-1 with the mnemonic No LASH, number of nodal sites, LDH, age, stage, and hemoglobin. FLIPI-2 replaces some of those with lymph node size, beta-2 microglobulin, and bone marrow involvement. Risk stratifies into low, intermediate, and high groups. And PRIMA-PI offers a quicker two-variable approach using beta-2 microglobulin and marrow involvement.
